_help: TI-99/4A GPL (Graphics Programming Language): the language of the console's own screens and of cartridge programs stored in GROM.
First draft: a small set of commands, to test that the extension reads GPL layout and memory-space operands (@, *, V@, V*, G@, #) correctly. More commands follow once this works.
name: TI-99/4A GPL (xga99)
about: TI's own internal language, run by the console one step at a time from GROM. Slower than machine code, but compact, and it is how the console's menus and many cartridges start.

registers.about: GPL has no registers. It works directly on memory: the console's fast 256-byte scratchpad (>8300 to >83FF), video memory and GROM.

build._about: How to build code for this chip. xga99 turns the .gpl file into a GROM image (name.gbc). There is no emulator step: a GROM image can't be started on its own.

tool.name: xga99
tool.why: turns GPL source into a GROM program
tool.get: Download the newest xdt99-<version>-Windows.zip (or the .zip for Mac and Linux) from the Releases page and unzip it into your tools folder. It also needs Python 3.

build.hint: Building makes a GROM image (name.gbc). To make a cartridge image for MAME instead, set "retroAsm.build.command" to something like python xga99.py -c "${file}".

operandForms.text: the {unit} in video memory at {e1} plus the number held at {e2}
operandForms.name: Video memory, with an offset
operandForms.help: V@ means video memory (the video chip's own 16K, where the screen lives). The number in brackets is the place that holds an offset to add to the address.

operandForms.name: Video memory
operandForms.help: V@ means video memory: the video chip's own 16K, where everything on screen lives.

operandForms.text: the {unit} in video memory at the address held in {e1}
operandForms.name: Video memory, address kept in memory
operandForms.help: The place after V* holds an address. The instruction uses the video memory at that address.

operandForms.text: the {unit} in GROM at {e1} plus the number held at {e2}
operandForms.name: GROM, with an offset
operandForms.help: G@ means GROM, the read-only chips. It can only be used with MOVE.

operandForms.name: GROM
operandForms.help: G@ means GROM: the read-only chips that hold the console's and cartridges' GPL. It can only be used with MOVE.

operandForms.name: Video chip setting
operandForms.help: One of the video chip's 8 settings (screen mode, colours, where its tables are kept). Only allowed as the destination of MOVE.

operandForms.text: the {unit} at the address held in {e1}, plus the number held at {e2}
operandForms.name: Memory, address kept in memory, with an offset
operandForms.help: The place after * holds an address. The number in brackets is added to it first.

operandForms.text: the {unit} at the address held in {e1}
operandForms.name: Memory, address kept in memory
operandForms.help: The place after * holds an address (a pointer). The instruction uses the memory at that address, not the place itself.

operandForms.text: the {unit} at {e1} plus the number held at {e2}
operandForms.name: Memory, with an offset
operandForms.help: The address is the one in front, plus whatever number is held at the place in brackets. Used to pick one entry out of a table.

operandForms.name: Memory at a fixed address
operandForms.help: The @ means the memory at this address (the console's fast scratchpad or the cartridge's RAM). Without the @ you would get the number itself.

instructions._help: Source comes first, then destination, as in ST value,place. D in front of a name (DST, DADD ...) works on a word (2 bytes) instead of a byte.

ST.name: Store a byte
ST.summary: Puts a byte into a place. The value can be a number or the byte from somewhere else. The source is not changed.

DST.name: Store a word
DST.summary: Puts a word (2 bytes) into a place. The same as ST, but for 2 bytes.

MOVE.name: Move a block of bytes
MOVE.summary: Copies a run of bytes from one place to another. It can reach CPU memory (@), video memory (V@), GROM (G@) and the video chip's settings (#), which makes it the way to fill the screen's graphics from a cartridge.
MOVE.more: The count is a number (or a place that holds one). GROM can be read from but not written to, and # settings can only be written to.

EX.name: Exchange bytes
EX.summary: Swaps the bytes held in two places.

DDEC.name: Subtract 1 from a word
DDEC.summary: Takes 1 away from a word (2 bytes).

ADD.name: Add bytes
ADD.summary: Adds the value to the byte in the place. The value is not changed.

DADD.name: Add words
DADD.summary: Adds the value to the word (2 bytes) in the place. The value is not changed.

SUB.name: Subtract bytes
SUB.summary: Takes the value away from the byte in the place. The value is not changed.

DSUB.name: Subtract words
DSUB.summary: Takes the value away from the word (2 bytes) in the place. The value is not changed.

CEQ.name: Compare: equal?
CEQ.summary: Asks whether two bytes are the same. The answer is kept as a yes/no that the next BS or BR can act on.

CZ.name: Compare: zero?
CZ.summary: Asks whether a byte is 0. The answer is kept as a yes/no that the next BS or BR can act on.

BR.name: Branch if the test said no
BR.explain: Jump to {1} if the last test came out no.
BR.summary: Jumps to the label if the last test came out no. Otherwise carries on. The label must be in the same 8K GROM as the jump.
BR.more: BR stands for branch if reset. It reads the yes/no left by the last compare.

BS.name: Branch if the test said yes
BS.explain: Jump to {1} if the last test came out yes.
BS.summary: Jumps to the label if the last test came out yes. Otherwise carries on. The label must be in the same 8K GROM as the jump.
BS.more: BS stands for branch if set. It reads the yes/no left by the last compare.

B.name: Branch (always)
B.summary: Always jumps to the label, wherever it is in GROM.

CALL.name: Call a routine
CALL.summary: Runs the routine at the label, then comes back to the next line when it reaches RTN.

RTN.name: Return
RTN.summary: Ends a routine and goes back to the line after the CALL.

RTNC.name: Return, keeping the test result
RTNC.summary: Like RTN, but the yes/no left by the last test is kept, so the caller can act on it.
RTNC.explain: Return to the caller, keeping the test result.

XML.name: Run machine code
XML.summary: Hands over to a machine-code routine. The number is two digits: the first picks a list of routines, the second picks one from that list. For lists 7, 8 and 9 the routines are in the cartridge's ROM.
XML.explain: Run the machine-code routine picked by {1}.

SCAN.name: Scan the keyboard
SCAN.summary: Checks the keyboard (and joysticks) once. The key code is left at >8375 (>FF means no key).

ALL.name: Fill the screen
ALL.summary: Fills the whole screen with one character.

BACK.name: Set the screen colour
BACK.summary: Sets the colour of the screen's border and background.

RAND.name: Random number
RAND.summary: Puts a random number at >8378. With a limit, the number is below it.
RAND.explain: Pick a random number and leave it at >8378.

I/O.name: Input or output
I/O.summary: Does an input or output job. The first number says which kind. Most often used to start a list of sounds playing.

EXIT.name: Exit to the title screen
EXIT.summary: Stops the program and goes back to the console's title screen.

HTEXT.name: Write text across
HTEXT.summary: Writes the text onto the screen from the current row and column, going across.

VTEXT.name: Write text down
VTEXT.summary: Writes the text onto the screen from the current row and column, going down.

HCHAR.name: Repeat a character across
HCHAR.summary: Draws one character the given number of times, going across.

VCHAR.name: Repeat a character down
VCHAR.summary: Draws one character the given number of times, going down.

ROW.name: Set the row
ROW.summary: Says which screen row the next drawing starts on (the top row is 0).

COL.name: Set the column
COL.summary: Says which screen column the next drawing starts in (the left column is 0).

ROW+.name: Move down some rows
ROW+.summary: Moves the drawing position down by that many rows.

COL+.name: Move right some columns
COL+.summary: Moves the drawing position right by that many columns.

H.name: Test: higher?
H.summary: Records as yes or no whether the last comparison said "higher", so the next BS or BR can act on it.

GT.name: Test: greater than?
GT.summary: Records as yes or no whether the last comparison said "greater than", so the next BS or BR can act on it.

CARRY.name: Test: carry?
CARRY.summary: Records as yes or no whether the last calculation carried out, so the next BS or BR can act on it.

OVF.name: Test: overflow?
OVF.summary: Records as yes or no whether the last calculation overflowed, so the next BS or BR can act on it.

CH.name: Compare bytes: higher?
CH.summary: Asks whether the byte in the place is higher than the value, treating both as plain positive numbers. The answer is kept as a yes/no for BS or BR.

CHE.name: Compare bytes: higher or equal?
CHE.summary: Asks whether the byte in the place is higher than or equal to the value, treating both as plain positive numbers. The answer is kept as a yes/no for BS or BR.
CHE.explain: Test whether {2} is higher than or equal to {1}.

CGT.name: Compare bytes: greater than?
CGT.summary: Asks whether the byte in the place is greater than the value, treating both as numbers that can be negative. The answer is kept as a yes/no for BS or BR.
CGT.explain: Test whether {2} is greater than {1}, allowing negative numbers.

CGE.name: Compare bytes: greater or equal?
CGE.summary: Asks whether the byte in the place is greater than or equal to the value, treating both as numbers that can be negative. The answer is kept as a yes/no for BS or BR.
CGE.explain: Test whether {2} is greater than or equal to {1}, allowing negative numbers.

CLOG.name: Compare bits: bytes
CLOG.summary: Combines the two values with AND (neither is changed) and records whether the result is 0. Used to ask whether certain bits are off.
CLOG.explain: Test the bits of {2} picked by {1}.

DCEQ.name: Compare words: equal?
DCEQ.summary: Asks whether two words (2 bytes each) are the same. The answer is kept as a yes/no that the next BS or BR can act on.

DCH.name: Compare words: higher?
DCH.summary: Asks whether the word in the place is higher than the value, treating both as plain positive numbers. The answer is kept as a yes/no for BS or BR.

DCHE.name: Compare words: higher or equal?
DCHE.summary: Asks whether the word in the place is higher than or equal to the value, treating both as plain positive numbers. The answer is kept as a yes/no for BS or BR.
DCHE.explain: Test whether {2} is higher than or equal to {1}.

DCGT.name: Compare words: greater than?
DCGT.summary: Asks whether the word in the place is greater than the value, treating both as numbers that can be negative. The answer is kept as a yes/no for BS or BR.
DCGT.explain: Test whether {2} is greater than {1}, allowing negative numbers.

DCGE.name: Compare words: greater or equal?
DCGE.summary: Asks whether the word in the place is greater than or equal to the value, treating both as numbers that can be negative. The answer is kept as a yes/no for BS or BR.
DCGE.explain: Test whether {2} is greater than or equal to {1}, allowing negative numbers.

DCLOG.name: Compare bits: words
DCLOG.summary: Combines the two values with AND (neither is changed) and records whether the result is 0. Used to ask whether certain bits are off.
DCLOG.explain: Test the bits of {2} picked by {1}.

DCZ.name: Compare: word is zero?
DCZ.summary: Asks whether a word (2 bytes) is 0. The answer is kept as a yes/no for BS or BR.

CASE.name: Pick a jump by number
CASE.summary: Uses the number in the place to choose one of the jump instructions listed straight after it, a quick way to pick between several choices.
CASE.explain: Jump to the entry picked by {1} in the list below.

DCASE.name: Pick a jump by number (word)
DCASE.summary: Like CASE, but the number is a word (2 bytes).
DCASE.explain: Jump to the entry picked by {1} in the list below.

MUL.name: Multiply bytes
MUL.summary: Multiplies the byte in the place by the value. The answer can be bigger than the place can hold, so it uses the bytes after it too.

DIV.name: Divide bytes
DIV.summary: Divides the number in the place by the value. The answer and the remainder are kept in the place and the bytes after it.

ABS.name: Make a byte positive
ABS.summary: Turns a negative byte into the matching positive one. A positive one is left alone.

NEG.name: Change the sign of a byte
NEG.summary: Turns a positive byte into the matching negative one, and the other way round.

INV.name: Flip every bit of a byte
INV.summary: Turns every 1 bit into 0 and every 0 bit into 1.

AND.name: AND bytes
AND.summary: Keeps only the bits that are 1 in both the value and the place. Handy for picking out some bits.
AND.explain: Keep only the bits of {2} that are also set in {1}.

OR.name: OR bytes
OR.summary: Turns on every bit in the place that is 1 in the value.
OR.explain: Turn on the bits of {2} that are set in {1}.

XOR.name: XOR bytes
XOR.summary: Flips every bit in the place that is 1 in the value.
XOR.explain: Flip the bits of {2} that are set in {1}.

SLL.name: Shift left (byte)
SLL.summary: Slides the bits of the byte to the left by that many places, filling with 0s on the right. Each place doubles the number.

SRL.name: Shift right (byte)
SRL.summary: Slides the bits of the byte to the right by that many places, filling with 0s on the left. Each place halves the number.

SRA.name: Shift right, keep the sign (byte)
SRA.summary: Like SRL, but a negative number stays negative: the sign bit is copied in on the left.
SRA.explain: Shift {2} right by {1} places, keeping its sign.

SRC.name: Rotate right (byte)
SRC.summary: Slides the bits to the right, and the ones that fall off the right end come back in on the left.

DMUL.name: Multiply words
DMUL.summary: Multiplies the word in the place by the value. The answer can be bigger than the place can hold, so it uses the bytes after it too.

DDIV.name: Divide words
DDIV.summary: Divides the number in the place by the value. The answer and the remainder are kept in the place and the bytes after it.

DABS.name: Make a word positive
DABS.summary: Turns a negative word into the matching positive one. A positive one is left alone.

DNEG.name: Change the sign of a word
DNEG.summary: Turns a positive word into the matching negative one, and the other way round.

DINV.name: Flip every bit of a word
DINV.summary: Turns every 1 bit into 0 and every 0 bit into 1.

DAND.name: AND words
DAND.summary: Keeps only the bits that are 1 in both the value and the place. Handy for picking out some bits.
DAND.explain: Keep only the bits of {2} that are also set in {1}.

DOR.name: OR words
DOR.summary: Turns on every bit in the place that is 1 in the value.
DOR.explain: Turn on the bits of {2} that are set in {1}.

DXOR.name: XOR words
DXOR.summary: Flips every bit in the place that is 1 in the value.
DXOR.explain: Flip the bits of {2} that are set in {1}.

DSLL.name: Shift left (word)
DSLL.summary: Slides the bits of the word to the left by that many places, filling with 0s on the right. Each place doubles the number.

DSRL.name: Shift right (word)
DSRL.summary: Slides the bits of the word to the right by that many places, filling with 0s on the left. Each place halves the number.

DSRA.name: Shift right, keep the sign (word)
DSRA.summary: Like SRL, but a negative number stays negative: the sign bit is copied in on the left.
DSRA.explain: Shift {2} right by {1} places, keeping its sign.

DSRC.name: Rotate right (word)
DSRC.summary: Slides the bits to the right, and the ones that fall off the right end come back in on the left.

DEX.name: Exchange words
DEX.summary: Swaps the words (2 bytes each) held in two places.

PUSH.name: Push a byte onto the data stack
PUSH.summary: Puts a byte onto the data stack, a pile of values the program can add to and take off again.

FETCH.name: Read the next program byte
FETCH.summary: Reads the next byte of the program itself, instead of running it as a command, and puts it in the place. Lets a program carry small pieces of data inline.
FETCH.explain: Read the next byte of the program into {1}.

COINC.name: Check for overlap
COINC.summary: Coincidence test: asks whether two things on the screen overlap. The answer is kept as a yes/no for BS or BR.

PARSE.name: BASIC: parse
PARSE.summary: Used by the BASIC language inside the console. Cartridge programs do not normally use it.

CONT.name: BASIC: continue
CONT.summary: Used by the BASIC language inside the console. Cartridge programs do not normally use it.

EXEC.name: BASIC: execute
EXEC.summary: Used by the BASIC language inside the console. Cartridge programs do not normally use it.

RTNB.name: BASIC: return
RTNB.summary: Used by the BASIC language inside the console. Cartridge programs do not normally use it.

SWGR.name: Undocumented
SWGR.summary: TI never documented this one. xga99 knows it and a few programs use it. Its exact job is not confirmed here.

DSWGR.name: Undocumented (word)
DSWGR.summary: TI never documented this one. xga99 knows it and a few programs use it. Its exact job is not confirmed here.

RTGR.name: Undocumented
RTGR.summary: TI never documented this one. xga99 knows it and a few programs use it. Its exact job is not confirmed here.

HSTR.name: Write text from memory across
HSTR.summary: Writes that many characters, taken from a place in memory, onto the screen going across.

HMOVE.name: Write text from memory across
HMOVE.summary: Writes that many characters, taken from a place in memory, onto the screen going across.

BIAS.name: Shift character numbers
BIAS.summary: Sets a number that is added to every character drawn after it. Lets the same text use a different set of character shapes.

RB.name: Turn a bit off
RB.summary: Turns bit number 0 to 7 of the byte in the place off (to 0). An xga99 shortcut that is written out as an AND.

SB.name: Turn a bit on
SB.summary: Turns bit number 0 to 7 of the byte in the place on (to 1). An xga99 shortcut that is written out as an OR.

TBR.name: Test a bit
TBR.summary: Tests one bit (0 to 7) of the byte in the place and records the answer as a yes/no for BS or BR. An xga99 shortcut that is written out as a CLOG.

HOME.name: Back to the top left
HOME.summary: Sets the screen-drawing position back to row 0, column 0. An xga99 shortcut that clears the row and column places (YPT and XPT).
HOME.explain: Move the drawing position to the top left.

EQU.name: Equate
EQU.summary: Gives a name to a number. It takes up no space in the program.

DATA.name: Word data
DATA.summary: Puts words (2 bytes each, left byte first) into the program at this point.

BYTE.name: Byte data
BYTE.summary: Puts single bytes into the program at this point.

TEXT.name: Text
TEXT.summary: Puts the letters of some text into the program, one byte per letter.

STRI.name: Text with its length first
STRI.summary: Like TEXT, but with a byte in front that says how long the text is.

BSS.name: Reserve space
BSS.summary: Leaves a gap of that many bytes in the program. The label is the address of the first byte.

GROM.name: Start of a GROM
GROM.summary: Says which GROM the following code goes in. Each GROM holds 8K of address space: GROM 3 starts at >6000 on a cartridge.

AORG.name: Place the code
AORG.summary: Places the following code at that offset inside the current GROM (from >0000 to >1FFF).

FMT.name: Start a screen-drawing block
FMT.summary: Starts a block of screen-drawing commands (HTEXT, ROW, COL ...). The block ends at FEND.

FOR.name: Repeat inside FMT
FOR.summary: Starts a part of a screen-drawing block that is repeated that many times. Ends at FEND.

FEND.name: End of FMT or FOR
FEND.summary: Ends the nearest FOR, or the FMT block if there is no FOR open.

COPY.name: Copy in another file
COPY.summary: Pulls in another source file at this point.

END.name: End of source
END.summary: Marks the end of the source.

TITLE.name: Program title
TITLE.summary: Sets the program's title (the first 12 letters are used).

FLOAT.name: Floating-point number
FLOAT.summary: Puts a number in the TI's 8-byte floating-point format into the program.

BCOPY.name: Copy in a binary file
BCOPY.summary: Pulls in the raw bytes of another file at this point.

PAGE.name: Listing page break
PAGE.summary: Starts a new page in the listing. Does not affect the program.

LIST.name: Listing on
LIST.summary: Turns the listing back on. Does not affect the program.

UNL.name: Listing off
UNL.summary: Turns the listing off. Does not affect the program.

LISTM.name: Macro listing on
LISTM.summary: Shows macro lines in the listing. Does not affect the program.

UNLM.name: Macro listing off
UNLM.summary: Hides macro lines from the listing. Does not affect the program.

.IFDEF.name: If defined (xga99)
.IFDEF.summary: Only assemble the lines that follow (up to .else or .endif) if this name exists.

.IFNDEF.name: If not defined (xga99)
.IFNDEF.summary: Only assemble the lines that follow if this name does not exist.

.ELSE.name: Otherwise (xga99)
.ELSE.summary: Starts the lines to assemble when the .if test was false.

.DEFM.name: Define macro (xga99)
.DEFM.summary: Starts a macro: a named group of lines you can reuse by writing .NAME. Inside it, #1, #2 ... stand for the values passed in.

symbols._help: Names xga99 already knows, so a program can use them without defining them.

MAXMEM.text: xga99 name for >8370: the top of the usable video memory.

DATSTK.text: xga99 name for >8372: where the data stack pointer is kept.

SUBSTK.text: xga99 name for >8373: where the subroutine stack pointer is kept.

KEYBRD.text: xga99 name for >8374: the keyboard mode used by SCAN.

KEY.text: xga99 name for >8375: the key SCAN found (>FF = none).

JOYY.text: xga99 name for >8376: joystick up/down, set by SCAN.

JOYX.text: xga99 name for >8377: joystick left/right, set by SCAN.

RANDOM.text: xga99 name for >8378: the random number from RAND.

TIMER.text: xga99 name for >8379: a counter that goes up with the screen refresh.

MOTION.text: xga99 name for >837A: sprite motion count.

VDPSTT.text: xga99 name for >837B: a copy of the video chip status.

STATUS.text: xga99 name for >837C: the GPL status byte (bit >20 is the yes/no from the last test).

CB.text: xga99 name for >837D: the cursor-blink counter.

YPT.text: xga99 name for >837E: the row the screen-drawing commands are at.

XPT.text: xga99 name for >837F: the column the screen-drawing commands are at.

FAC.text: xga99 name for >834A: the floating-point accumulator.

ARG.text: xga99 name for >835C: the second floating-point number.

ERCODE.text: xga99 name for >8354: the error code.

VPAB.text: xga99 name for >8356: the pointer to the file description in video memory.

VSTACK.text: xga99 name for >836E: the value stack pointer.

addresses._help: The console's fast scratchpad memory, as GPL programs see it.
addresses.8374: Keyboard mode: which part of the keyboard SCAN looks at. 0 = whole keyboard.
addresses.8375: The key SCAN found. >FF means no key was pressed.
addresses.8379: A counter that goes up with the screen refresh (60 times a second).
addresses.837C: The status byte: bit >20 is the yes/no left by the last test.
addresses.837E: The row the screen-drawing commands are at.
addresses.837F: The column the screen-drawing commands are at.
